Publish from Spline (and put the link in Figma)#

**Status: 4.0.0-beta.1 — the Spline path works today through the existing uploaders; the Figma plug-in is a skeleton. Spline has no editor plug-in API**, so there is no Verse button inside Spline. A GLB exported from Spline publishes like any GLB. The Figma plug-in's Insert a Verse link works with any server; its Publish a GLB uses an upload core that was tested in Node against a real local Verse server (one-shot, resumable, resize, dead server, cancel; web/test/fix-verify-aec.mjs), but **from inside Figma it needs the server to accept cross-origin uploads, which today's server does not** (below). Nothing has been run inside Figma yet.

Spline → Verse#

  1. In Spline: Export ▸ 3D formats ▸ glTF and download the binary .glb (a multi-file .gltf must be zipped with its files, or re-exported as GLB).
  2. Publish the file, any of these ways:
    • drop it on the Verse upload screen in the browser;
    • python3 integrations/aec/shared/python/verse_upload.py scene.glb --server https://verse.ctruh.com (prints the link; --open opens it);
    • the Figma plug-in below, if your server accepts uploads from it.
  3. Check the size with the viewer's measure tool. Spline does not state a unit for its scenes; if the object comes out far too large, publish again from the Figma plug-in with Size ▸ 1 unit = 1 cm (÷100) (or ÷1000). This wraps the scene in one scale node; nothing else changes.

Spline-only features — states, events, interactions, the Spline runtime's materials — are not part of a GLB and do not come across. Plain PBR materials and textures do.

1. Install the Figma plug-in#

  1. Download VersePublish-Figma-4.0.0-beta.1.zip from the downloads page (or build it: sh integrations/aec/figma/make_package.sh) and unzip it.
  2. In the Figma desktop app: **Plugins ▸ Development ▸ Import plugin from manifest…** and pick manifest.json.
  3. Run Plugins ▸ Development ▸ Verse Publish; set the server URL (and an API key / account token if you have them).

Success looks like: Insert a Verse link puts the link on the canvas as hyperlinked text; clicking it opens the 3D scene in the browser.

The Figma plug-in#

Figma is a 2D tool; the useful thing a plug-in can do is put the 3D link on the canvas next to the design.

  • Insert a Verse link: paste a link, it lands on the canvas as hyperlinked text. Works today.
  • Publish a GLB (for example a Spline export) with a Size choice, progress and Cancel, then insert its link. **Blocked on the server today:** a Figma plug-in's UI runs with origin null, and an upload with Verse's headers needs a CORS preflight; OPTIONS /v1/ingest answers 404 without Access-Control-* headers. Allowing cross-origin uploads to /v1/ingest* is a product and security decision (any web page could then upload from a visitor's browser), so it has not been changed. Until it is, the plug-in says: "Could not reach the Verse server … (From Figma this also happens when the server does not accept uploads from plug-ins …)".

Settings. Figma sandboxes plug-ins, so the plug-in cannot read the settings.json the desktop plug-ins share; its server URL, API key and token are kept in Figma's per-user plug-in storage (figma.clientStorage). A self-hosted server must also be added to networkAccess.allowedDomains in manifest.json.

Troubleshooting#

Every problem ends in one sentence; the first words tell you which row applies.

You seeWhat it meansDo this
"Could not reach the Verse server at … (From Figma this also happens when the server does not accept uploads from plug-ins …)"From inside Figma: the server does not accept cross-origin uploads (true of verse.ctruh.com today). Otherwise a wrong URL or no internet.Publish the GLB with the upload card or verse_upload.py and use Insert a Verse link; check the server URL.
"The Verse server at … did not recognise the account token …"The token is mistyped, revoked, or from another server. Nothing was uploaded.Copy it again from Studio, or clear it.
"The server did not accept your API key or account token …"The server only takes uploads with an API key.Enter the key from the server's operator.
"Upload limit reached: …"The hourly upload limit, or the key's daily quota.Wait as the sentence says, or add an account token.
"The server is busy right now. …" / "The server is out of storage. …"The server's build queue or disk is full. Your file is fine.Publish again in a few minutes.
"Only a binary glTF (.glb) can be resized here."Size was set for a file that is not a GLB.Export GLB from Spline, or publish at the exported size.
"Verse cannot build … files yet. Export the model as GLB (or FBX / OBJ) and publish that file instead."A STEP / CAD file was picked.Export GLB and publish that.
The model is 100× too bigSpline wrote centimetres.Publish again with Size ▸ 1 unit = 1 cm (÷100).
